description: Semantic contract edges for the impact proof-cone selector (developer-velocity epic V4a). Production paths declare the contracts they own; tests declare the contracts they exercise. Changing a contract-owning path selects every test claiming that contract. Unknown or undeclared contracts fail closed. This manifest is EXPLICIT and hand-curated; static dependency and coverage relationships are generated and live elsewhere. Every owner/test path must exist in the tree (directory prefix or file); dead edges are a contract defect.

distributed-transaction-coordinator-part.description: The query coordinator and partition participant share one TX1 revision-10 identity, manifest, prepare evidence, immutable decision and typed-answer protocol. Every coordinator-managed transaction prepares before one decision; a recorded COMMIT only moves forward, and recovery re-drives the exact recorded decision.

transaction-workflow-recovery-ownership.description: The workflow registry retains restart obligations by immutable workflow ID and preserves an existing live owner binding. Query request and recovery work share one session FIFO and complete only their exact transaction identity.

wit-world-interface.description: The WIT world/component interface shape; every WASM service consumer depends on it.

message-envelope.description: Inter-node message envelope/codec and transport contract.

partition-topology.description: Partition topology, split/merge, and placement contracts.

replica-operation-state.description: Replica-operation state machine and terminal-CAS contract.

sql-grammar.description: SQL grammar and statement parser contract.

seed-registration-election-scheduling.description: Seed registration's direct-write leader dependency cut and the partition election scheduler share one transferred leadership gate.

quest-solver-ledger.description: Solver event log, Quest store, and landing/verification contract.

priority-spread-planner-admission.description: Priority spread-cure retention and coordinator admission remain mutually compatible.

priority-services-publication-census.description: Priority SERVICES-row publication supplies every field required by the membership census.

priority-services-marker-reconcile.description: Local-only SERVICES-row marker clearing and reconciliation converge as one retry contract.

replica-durable-generation-cleanup.description: Exact durable replica generations, SERVICES-key cleanup ownership, storage deletion, startup admission, and live-row creation form one lifecycle closure contract.

failed-create-target-authoritative-clean.description: OperationWorkflowOwner alone admits failed create terminalization and cleanup from an exact authoritative lifecycle generation, persists that decision through ReplicaOperationRepository, and re-drives lifecycle-owner release without accepting cache projection as authority.

critical-create-admission-topology-order.description: Critical create admission runs before the downstream topology guard on createOperation.

readiness-versioned-planning-liveness.description: Node-liveness semantic projection, complete-token readiness freshness, macrotask-bounded planning, and non-recursive readiness-internal owner reads form one convergence contract.

active-gate-convergence.description: The canonical active-gate system contract: the control-plane read gateway derives complete-table evidence only from a serving-leader witness, authoritative discovery repair pressure containment and startup ACTIVE convergence stay compatible, the membership-publication owner remains re-entrant and follows live write leadership across fail-back, callers cannot bypass failed-repair backoff, and stale deferred evidence cannot become a permanent ACTIVE veto after newer owner evidence exists.

admin-cache-owner-lifecycle.description: The Admin WebSocket notification subscription and its cache-bound snapshot and repair children transition one coherent read/mutation cache owner pair: same-owner binding is idempotent, handoff generation-fences in-flight and reusable state, and serialized shutdown/restart cannot strand or resurrect a listener.

operation-ledger-self-move-interlock.description: The operation-ledger self-move interlock: hold registration at createOperation, engagement at the dispatching owner's PENDING -> SENDING claim (a foreign holder resolved through the authoritative lifecycle read), and release only by the holder's own terminal row stay one owner contract across the hold policy, the hold state, the admission lanes and the dispatch gate.

formation-release-handoff.description: The seed-owned formation-release handoff: the seed captures, retains and revokes a JOINING cohort generation and publishes a durable release contract; joiners consume it through a typed CONSUMER validation role and release their formation barrier from the whole-plane authority answer, never minting release authority, so the seed authority, the contract/evidence/publication projection and the joiner consumer barrier stay one owner contract.

raft-formation-attribution.description: Formation diagnostics owns the semantic mapping of consensus protocol work to raft_protocol and committed-apply work to raft_apply; the mapping is exclusive, restores callers, and is backend-neutral.

sql-engine-system-table-read.description: System-table reads answered by the SQL engine reflect rows written through the CDC owner; the engine is real on a production-booted node and a contract-bound seam in the membership-consistency harness.

CL-041.description: A follower grants its vote to at most one candidate per term, so at most one leader can be elected per term (Raft §5.2 Election Safety).

CL-040.description: A committed Raft log entry is identical cluster-wide at its index; a follower never stale-commits its own same-index/different-term entry on catch-up (Raft §5.3 Log Matching).

CL-042.description: An empty raft log's last-log-term is 0 (Raft §5.4.1): the consensus core never masquerades an empty log as up-to-date, so a voter holding committed entries denies an empty-log candidate regardless of the candidate's election term (CL-042).

CL-038.description: A surplus-drain REPLACE whose declared source replica is already removed terminalizes (reaches SAFE) instead of re-dispatching a source-leader handoff to a replica that no longer exists (CL-038).

CL-035.description: A replica's committed learner-to-voter raft promotion is seeded into its own node's local SERVICES row at voter-ready activation, so the REPLACE remove-safety gate observes the promotion instead of deferring on a stale learner/null raft_role forever (CL-035).

CL-033.description: The priority-recovery planning projection is memoized per publisher node (build once, reuse while the source revision and stale-grace window hold), so the post-restart recovery hot path cannot rebuild the heavy projection per call and freeze the control-plane seed's event loop past the raft election timeout (CL-033).

CL-034.description: The stage-3 membership-publication planning-snapshot merge (the residual readiness-build cost CL-033's projection memo does not cover) is memoized per publisher node under the same planning-source revision discipline, so per-routing-call rebuild storms cannot freeze the control-plane seed's event loop past the raft election timeout during recovery (CL-034).

CL-001.description: The strict-mode active-node projection retains an already-published node that is transport-alive and within the heartbeat grace through a transient heartbeat-stall trough, while never promoting a non-baseline node on that grace and still trimming a published node that is genuinely stale (CL-001 variant C).

golden-capability-gold-plating.description: A failed or unavailable authoritative read never concludes the positive premise of a safety gate: admission gates fail closed into a typed defer/deny (the conflict-lane deferred-visibility throw; the topology guard's replica_inventory_unusable denial; the surplus REMOVE commit fence; the ledger quorum-spread confirmation). A hold may fail OPEN on a read gap only where blocking on the gap would itself deadlock convergence, and each fail-open hold names its deadlock witness: the over-target count-keyed create-lane hold (G1; fail-closing it would strand the surplus drain it exists to release) and the routine-direction ledger self-move serialization (a disruptive IDLE_ONLY self-move still fails closed). Advisory probes fail open only where a fail-closed enforcer remains downstream (the provisioning ledger-interlock probe defers to operation creation as the enforcing seam).

publication-readiness-churn-liveness-clo.description: After semantic-input quiescence the final complete token is published; during continuous churn completed tokens advance monotonically, dirty owners receive bounded round-robin service, and stale evidence never promotes readiness. Continuous readiness source churn starts at most one heavy planning build globally per macrotask turn and permits a timer or heartbeat sentinel between every pair of heavy items.

architecture-model-chain.description: Executable architecture models are checks: an Alloy assertion, a decision-table rule or an owner-trace violation named by an invariant is validated and run by the model:contracts chain (the ci run's health steps on every main push) and by these tests locally, so a model or registry edit selects the chain.

readiness-handoff-liveness.description: Startup readiness is a controller handoff: the seed registers ready only after its canonical system leaders are in its cache AND its query/data-plane transport is serviceable, and a deferred handoff terminates (ready or blocked with a typed wake) within the bound the owner reports.

core-system-logic.description: The runtime invariants the core-system-logic contract cites (its architecture invariants bind through the Alloy, decision-table and owner-trace checks instead): a stale projection promotes no readiness lane, degraded runtime authority explains but never projects a node, and the seed phase owner transfers the control-plane writers to the steady-state owners on completion.

rolling-restart-rebalancer-handoff.description: The operation-workflow owner bounds deferred re-entry of a coordinator-created remote handoff per operation: retries re-arm with at least the minimum backoff and stop, clearing the retry, once the step has timed out and the operation budget (createdAt + REBALANCE_OPERATION_BUDGET_MS) has passed. Per operation only; the cross-operation cycle is formation-sim's question.

raft-rs-runtime-lifecycle-entry.description: The replica lifecycle owner admits each semantic operation before the runtime owner can enter the raft-rs core, and durable retirement waits for admitted operations before becoming terminal. A constructor refused before runtime admission publishes no membership reservation owner or native handle; each service initialization retains the exact named consensus failure and releases its own opening resources before reporting refusal. Exact-incarnation native opening history is NEVER_OPENED or ESTABLISHED in the existing lifecycle row; legacy NULL is unknown. Bootstrap and establishment commit atomically at FULL before participation; intact history restores, while absent native state cannot reopen an established or unknown incarnation. Host prior-existence remains independent for complete storage loss. If startup cleanup also fails, the original typed refusal and immutable owner retry answer remain primary; the actual secondary failure is retained, exact unclosed resources remain with the service lifecycle, initialize stays held, and existing shutdown retries that same cleanup without a new scheduler. Failed WASM teardown is CLEANUP_REQUIRED, not STOPPED. Each runtime turn captures its finite inbound extent after successful execution admission, checks current execution before dequeue, and leaves later accepted envelopes with the existing queue and owned wake; no later arrival enlarges that captured extent.

raft-rs-runtime-application-transaction.description: Ready processing and the application transaction owner keep application effects, partition progress, raft-rs applied progress, ConfState and each statement's durable outcome coherent across host failure and reconstruction; failure scope follows failure class (a core failure replaces the runtime and resumes every group once, a host failure reconstructs its own group and touches no other group; a failure within one retry window of the last instant the previous one held the group is the same persisting failure, whatever its class and whether or not a reconstruction succeeded in between, so the group is reconstructed at most once per window while it persists - at most ceil(span / window) + 1 reconstructions over any span - and a failure more than one window after the last one starts afresh; a group healed inside a window serves again only after it, so its first write after a heal waits up to one window), a durable record that cannot be read where a group is opened or reconstructed (a missing table, SQLITE_IOERR, SQLITE_CORRUPT) is that group's own typed host failure of phase durable-record-read and never a throw, a record that lost a table is never recreated empty (the record's tables are created in one transaction of the store's own, whole or not at all, so a partial schema only ever comes from outside), a replica whose record cannot be read at open is refused at initialization, typed and naming the phase and the table, whatever its replica count (healing in place is for a group that fails while it runs), a throw the runtime did not type is contained by the port as the group's typed host failure, a group without a usable host announces no role so its partition does not lead, a reconstructed sole voter leads again, a retry is answered from its durable outcome, and the admission owner refuses before consensus (and before a session stages it) every command the application would refuse or never answer. Shared native replacement holds entry until every registered group is reconstructed or explicitly held; callbacks cannot use stale handles or cached healthy observations. A failed shared reload owns one captured clock and existing election-derived retry window, shared by all callers; caller changes cannot renew or bypass it. Resumption uses each existing group queue; close discharges exact-handle obligations and final close releases the shared retry record. The registered participant release recovery owner visits current hosted services once in registry order and stops at the first actual leader. With no leader, the write kernel canonical host-held classifier retains one partition observation debt at the existing RECOVERY_RETRY_MS cadence; status.retryAfterMs is never consumed. Ordinary followers and candidates remain event-driven; null or unclassifiable status is typed UNAVAILABLE without a self wake. The existing queue coalesces events, permits at most four running attempts, throttles unchanged reports, and clears pending/report state after the last service is removed. Held reports preserve the blocked group, replica and failure cause. A timer-registration failure visibly reports UNAVAILABLE and discharges the unscheduled debt until a real event. Only fresh leader, durable origin, measured build and canonical release facts may enter cutover; absent origin or build remains OPERATOR_REQUIRED. After ENABLE, one bounded passive applied-position observation per current replica waits on runtime publication under the original RPC and attempt deadlines; every wake re-reads canonical facts and grants no release authority. Runtime not-before, reconstruction and durable replay remain runtime-owned. Canonical pause/resume refuses handler shutdown, service shutdown or registry replacement before idempotent OPEN and final mutation; stale lifecycle remains CLOSED, while a wrong release ID against an otherwise valid current OPEN returns STALE without revoking it. Existing generation, term, configuration, runtime, drain and census fences remain mandatory; a wake never grants release authority. A failed nested control release retains only bounded own-data string observations of its missing fact, phase and reason; unavailable diagnostic detail cannot replace the original refusal or decide authority. Deadline expiry before dependent ENABLE leaves its admission closed without erasing a prior control origin; a new no-origin continuation requires current authorization. After a lost committed ENABLE answer and intact restart, missing current control keeps admission closed while the existing retry retains recovery responsibility. Seed registration acquisition and participant release run inside the existing registration phase and scheduler boundary, so an expired committed release still cleans every acquired registration resource. Failed cleanup reports a frozen observation alongside the unchanged primary refusal, retains exact failed service and SQL engine objects, and discharges only the object whose native shutdown and required handler retirement succeeded. Bootstrap shutdown joins its current attempt and retries a rejected attempt through the same cleanup owner. A retained committed origin survives cleanup but grants no missing SERVICES placement identity on the next actual startup.

partition-raft-operation-port.description: The raft-rs runtime is the partition's only consensus backend: PartitionService builds its operation-only port through the fixed raft-rs operation-port owner (no selection and no alternate runtime injection) and consumes semantic operations, typed outcomes and immutable snapshots without a live node/control graph; a refused campaign or peer admission is the port's typed answer, never reported as done; every write the replica did not take is answered by the write kernel's builders, typed with its entry: a pending write released when its replica stops leading, at its commit deadline or at shutdown with what the replica knows of it (outcome unknown once handed to consensus; not leader, deadline passed or service shut down otherwise), a proposal queue at capacity as backpressure with the queue's retry time, a proposal the port refused with the port's reason, and a router holding the answer routes it again by its code (an unknown outcome only under its own entryId); a group held on a contained unexpected throw is named once in the partition's log at error level with its message, and its end once at info.

partition-session-transaction-persistenc.description: A participant staging session never holds a SQLite transaction on the partition's shared connection: the leader classifies each current session statement with its staging classifier and validates it inside one synchronous transaction that replays the staged operations and always rolls back, so the rs-raft store's persistence admission never defers consensus because of a participant session and no session ending can erase a consensus row. PREPARE and the decision are committed participant commands proposed outside any session. The store still refuses every durable consensus write inside a foreign transaction it did not open; the runtime asks that admission before it enters the core and before every Ready, and the write path turns the refusal into a bounded deferral.

spread-cure-transition-authorization.description: The cure policy owner mints one exact-transition spread-cure authorization; the receiving learner decodes and states exactly that record.

partition-write-answer-retry-classificat.description: The partition write kernel (the answer's code) and the errors owner (its text) are the one owner of what may be done again with a write the partition did not take, and every consumer asks them, never a text of its own: the control plane's retry classification retries every answer but a host failure while proposing (a write whose outcome is unknown did not fail, so it is never recorded as a failed write) - by the kernel's code when it holds the answer, by the errors owner's texts when only a text reached it; a router that sends the write again without its entryId never does so for an unknown outcome - never by its text, and by its code only when it re-proposes under the write's own entryId, where the retry is idempotent.

committed-bootstrap-stamp.description: Every join bootstrap is one canonical own-data stamp read from the group leader before operation persistence, carried unchanged through creation, decoded at the target, and enforced by the raft-rs participation gate; rows remain discovery only and an unreadable or malformed distributed answer fails closed.

replace-owner-membership-observation.description: The REPLACE owner decides source removal, completion and its leadership handoff only from decoded replica consensus observations. The target is a wake and route; the deciding answer must be the leader's own applied-at-commit configuration and a majority of that configuration must corroborate its term and leader identity. The operation port announces applied membership, the partition and node layers relay it, and READ_REPLICA_MEMBERSHIP / RETIRE_REPLICA_PEER read or mutate through the port. Rows never decide membership.

public-application-database-seam.description: The public Application Database seam (createEmbeddedLagrange -> openApplicationDatabase -> query/transaction): public result shape, typed errors, statement policy, and behaviour through embedded processes. Process-directory custody is retained across failed startup or shutdown cleanup; startup preserves both the initiating failure and cleanup rejection. Failed teardown permits no new directory owner until actual native release or process death.

test-listener-port-block.description: A runtime's test listener ports are one allocator block whose admin and transport ports the listener-port model derives from the REST port (getTestListenerPorts); changing the allocator or the port model must re-run the block witness.

public-seam-durability-certification-sou.description: The fixed rs-raft partition construction path makes the provider-neutral public-seam durability scenario eligible as CANDIDATE; the scenario must not consult the retired provider-selection compatibility surface.

harness-docker-build-context.description: The distributed-harness image build context is derived from the Dockerfile's COPY sources; changing either must re-run the parity falsifier.

public-call-outcome-class.description: The call routing contract is the one owner of the public outcome class of a failed CALL (derived from its classification, the per-dispatch invoked flag and the invocation-level execution evidence the call invoker records); the lifecycle command owner's failure projection is the one place that class, retrySafe and the topology-free message reach the PostgreSQL wire, and the public seam proof observes them through a real pg client.

public-binding-two-partition-policy-shap.description: The public Binding fanout proof persists its exact table policy through TablePolicyService, and the production split/merge manager consumes that policy with live child metrics before the harness relies on two frozen partition identities.

partition-replication-start-authorizatio.description: Durable split or merge workflow records authorize exact source START identities; sender delivery classification and PartitionService execution handles preserve that authorization through physical execution.

storage-reservation-authoritative-adopti.description: The reservation lifecycle uses the deterministic operation-derived identity, write-if-absent insertion, and exact authoritative live operation plus ACTIVE reservation witnesses to converge a lost INSERT answer on one durable capacity hold without duplicating creation observations; temporary operation-authority loss retains that hold and one canonical owner retry which survives restart and remains gated before dispatch.

message-group-learner-authorization-cons.description: The existing repository observes exact issued ADD_LEARNER intent and current host-bound holder/recipient facts; the group-admission owner consumes that observation before reserving the permanent peer identity and invoking the semantic port. The native runtime alone decides term/configuration/lifecycle/generation freshness and proposes. This does not authenticate transport, settle the operation from a proposal reply, or grant CREATE.

message-group-learner-delivery-lifetime.description: The current socket/local delivery lifetime stays with RouterConnectionAuthorityOwner. The issued-learner consumer requires its host-only context; the existing native turn rechecks the same predicate after queueing and immediately before proposal. Revoking delivery does not cancel the durable issued action or prove global metadata atomicity. No physical CREATE is admitted.

message-group-committed-learner-origin.description: Existing committed application and permanent identity owners retain exact managed learner origin atomically; the queued historical read and versioned checkpoint validate that origin. Missing evidence remains unresolved; no current CREATE or reissue authority.

message-group-learner-outcome-recording.description: Same-turn native historical origin and committed membership witness feed one exact existing operation-row CAS; preserve terminal debt and old execution fences; current CREATE and successor issuance remain separate.

message-group-registered-learner-read.description: Actual registered recipient and retained workflow turn bind invoked callback/router, delivery and native lifetime through guarded repository submission; owned discovery (restart scan, periodic sweep, replicated-row wake) recovers membership debt by operation ID through the same recorder with an explicitly hosted witness. Preserve UNKNOWN after submission; no atomic lease/boot revocation or CREATE/successor permission.

snapshot-receiver-lifecycle-staging.description: Validated snapshot installation consumes a narrow, immutable receiver-local staging result from the existing replica lifecycle owner; it neither constructs that owner nor acquires runtime/retirement authority. The lifecycle owner preserves an exact active incarnation and refuses conflicting, retired or lifecycle-less surviving native history. Snapshot installation retains validation, CREATE authorization, staged-file custody, native reconstruction and atomic publication. Fresh CREATE also consumes read-only surviving-receiver admission before staging, final swap and STAGED recovery; existing receiver history is not replaceable by checkpoint validity alone.

replica-host-cleanup-custody.description: The existing host retains exact unreleased service objects independently of active routing. Failed CREATE/restart and host shutdown use the same instance cleanup owner; typed failure retains custody, retries do not retarget successors, and pending cleanup bounds replacement admission without granting CREATE or storage-deletion authority.

wasm-writer-v1-application-completion.description: Review-only v1 writer-slot contract: exact durable outcomes and generation/sequence fences join KV effects and applied progress; live publication follows afterCommit. Fixed slot state, explicit acknowledgment and caller durable CAS preserve exact replay. INIT must not let delayed old administration revive a writer after recreation; this prerequisite is currently HOLD and the recreation witness retains its counterexample. This registration is not implementation approval or F1 supersession.

service-instance-selection-resource-stat.description: R2 ServiceDefinitionsOwner metadata arbitration: immutable caller request and catalog lineage feed one exact conditional service_instances row mutation; bounded decisions/slots retain replay fences and successor exclusion. Component SQL proof does not supply native genesis, local retirement or event-driven lifecycle reentry.

service-consensus-original-intent-admiss.description: The existing lifecycle journal retains the immutable original binding/slot request before the instance owner may reserve it, then retains the exact returned token. Re-entry and process-loss recovery use that journal, not current-definition reconstruction or a new operation identity. Retained admission starts no physical resource and is not serving authority.

service-consensus-retained-native-bootst.description: The original CREATE journal retains full immutable intent, admission token and first-opening identity across the manager, adapter, runtime and instance-qualified native WASM owner. Common B, exact local file and resource token are validated before bootstrap. Native committed INIT and founding-membership evidence enable only the metadata owner PUBLISHED grant, durably recorded locally before serving. U1 v3 and addenda expose one physical CURRENT/ABSENT/DIFFERENT/UNAVAILABLE observation to fence canonical state and driver projections without changing physical .live custody. Exact retirement admission is registered before collaborator invocation, retains cleanup intent and is joined before directory release; reused operation IDs require the same full origin. One physical FINAL fact requires acknowledged CLOSED or exact RETIRED tombstone plus HISTORY_UNAVAILABLE. Physical finality does not complete the journal: the original operation retains STOPPED-projection and authoritative completion debt independently. A retained, absent, failed or stopped projection writer cannot supply completion. Bootstrap creates no nested journal or discovery publication; the existing runtime projector owns subsequent exact-instance discovery. C6 uses real native resources with component metadata/journal adapters; distributed metadata, production A5 retained-to-applied continuation, cross-node wake delivery and process-loss recovery remain separate evidence.

runtime-service-bound-creation-route.description: U1 v3 and its addenda make one PENDING/IN_PROGRESS journal observation into exact per-origin continuation plans under one irreversible handler lifetime. Known retained requests route by full origin before the current memo; collisions preserve all plans and expose CONTINUATION_PENDING. Bound CREATE, coordinator REMOVE and silent startup retirement share the existing canonical replica execution gate, including one bounded startup retirement observer and global request-ID conflict checks. Prompt CREATE acknowledgment precedes journal-only hydration; a wake never adopts its token. Matching qualifying wakes retain at most one bit per plan or ordinary HELD memo and reenter only after gate settlement and immediate physical CURRENT. Canonical handler/manager/driver state cannot be rewritten by a historical or stale origin. Physical FINAL, exact STOPPED projection and authoritative original-journal completion are separate ordered obligations; retained, failed, absent or stopped projection replies keep RETIRED_UNPROJECTED and its original debt. The C6 handler, restart and physical-custody witnesses cover this complete interaction; the real asynchronous projection receipt continuation remains activation A5. Legacy REMOVE consumes the original operation through the existing repository with OWNER_RPC_REQUIRED and requireAbsenceConfirmation; unavailable authority leaves cleanup retryable. Bootstrap passes that dispatch authority to the handler. An admitted generic removal retains its exact local memo until STOP settles and releases its own execution even when that memo is superseded. Handler and strict-dispatch witnesses cover this consumer contract with a scripted repository, not native authority execution. The bound REMOVE operation witness follows real RF3 publication through exact endpoint withdrawal, full-origin native retirement, successor grant refusal and failed-close custody/retry. Its component SQLite metadata and same-process transport do not certify cross-host authority or generic catalog activation.

participant-release-bounded-completion.description: The existing release client owns response-to-delay completion for fresh seed and fresh CREATE with one original authority and deadline. Callers retain prerequisites and clock substrates; nested control and operator retain the single-attempt primitive. The audit validates the exact guarded operation and caller correspondence.

original-retained-history-observation.description: The durable Raft owner validates required raw rows, exact applied/commit/retained frontiers, suffix coverage, terms and bytes before original preparation delegates application inspection and again at native construction. The participant byte/store owners observe canonical ENABLE commands across applied, committed-pending and local-uncommitted ranges in one read snapshot with the durable origin row, preserving legitimate repeats and every unclassified application effect. Neither observation writes, replays, truncates, grants full original-history acceptance or opens startup; checkpoint/configuration interpretation and SQL/MG effect permission remain explicit unavailable dependencies.

original-retained-effects-correspondence.description: Read-only original foundation correspondence consumes actual registration/SQL producers and application owners in one native/application snapshot. Exact SQL/params/rows, first statement outcomes, generation and complete owed/delivered CDC census must agree; applied ACKs bind first delivery and pending source dependencies remain unavailable. Physical schema belongs to the actual partition opener; no native DDL producer is inferred. Strict MG content observation preserves both stamps without source-occurrence authority. Startup and continuation remain held; this observation grants no opening or publication right.

cdc-source-native-delivery.description: Durable source CDC preserves the ordered semantic vector and source occurrence through the responsible subscriber, seed or joining bridge, topology wave and native committed application. The existing source invocation, topology progress, retry owner, transport clock/queue/write callback and native wait own response and actual cleanup separately. Only exact full-vector native afterCommit acceptance can authorize the source CDC_DELIVERED application; complete provisional coverage may release scanning while retaining debt. Named component, native and regression witnesses are registered for measurement, not claimed passing or sufficient for full W7/W9, startup classification, two-start acceptance or merge.

router-delivery-envelope.description: The router alone computes a delivery's transport outcome, from its own facts: an answer cannot change the acknowledgement (decision D2), a lost answer after the ACK is the router's deferral and never DELIVERED (F-A), a handler throw is FAILED/handler_failed on the LOCAL and the remote path alike (D1), and a no-handler reply is a frame-level router fact with no answer slot. Q6 stages 1-2 keep the flat shape; the {transport, answer} envelope cutover restates the approved C2 roundtrip and forwarding-hop witnesses and widens W-ENV-1 to every transport field.

distributed-transaction-coordinator-part.description: Coordinator decisions are bound to the PREPARE evidence participants answer, and participants apply only that bound decision and return exact durable outcomes.

transaction-workflow-recovery-ownership.description: Workflow restart ownership and query recovery preserve the same immutable workflow and owner identity across process loss.

seed-registration-election-scheduling.description: Registration owns the exact direct-write dependency cut and one wait budget; partition scheduling prioritizes that cut and releases all other elections without restating it.

priority-spread-planner-retention-admiss.description: The planner must retain the same over-target spread cure that coordinator admission permits.

priority-services-row-publication-census.description: Published priority SERVICES rows must satisfy the census field and readiness vocabulary.

priority-services-marker-reconcile.description: The durable-apply marker decision and retry reconciliation must preserve eventual SERVICES-row publication.

replica-durable-generation-cleanup.description: Lifecycle CAS, cleanup-key arbitration, physical storage deletion, and every storage-open admission must preserve one exact durable owner for a logical replica identity.

failed-create-target-authoritative-clean.description: OperationWorkflowOwner terminal admission and repair must carry the exact lifecycle generation through repository persistence and ReplicaHandler cleanup, while projections remain non-authoritative.

critical-create-hold-topology-guard-orde.description: Critical create admission must run before downstream topology checks consume its safety premise.

readiness-freshness-macrotask-bound.description: The readiness owner may reflect every final semantic token only through a globally macrotask-bounded heavy-work scheduler.

active-gate-authoritative-repair-backoff.description: Failed authoritative-repair backoff must remain non-bypassable while newer evidence or retry ownership can still re-drive the single startup ACTIVE decision owner.

admin-notification-repair-cache-owner-ha.description: Admin notification lifecycle transitions and cache-bound snapshot/repair state must observe the same cache owner generation, so shutdown cannot rebind delivery and an old repair completion or deferral cannot govern a replacement cache.

operation-ledger-self-move-hold-dispatch.description: The coordinator's hold registration/admission lanes and the workflow owner's self-move dispatch claim must keep agreeing on who holds the ledger self-move interlock: an engagement that refuses on a remembered holder without reading its row starves every re-planned self-move behind a terminal predecessor.

formation-release-seed-contract-joiner-c.description: The seed release authority and the joiner consumer/barrier must keep agreeing on a retained cohort generation: a consumer predicate that nulls a valid seed contract strands the cohort on the raw spread predicate (the 2026-08-28..30 class), so any change to either endpoint re-runs both formation-release witnesses.

sql-engine-cache-membership.description: The SQL engine and the system-table cache agree on membership rows: what the CDC owner writes, the engine reads back. Seamed in the membership-consistency harness, real in the seven-node probe.

raft-rs-runtime-lifecycle-entry.description: Lifecycle admission and core entry must remain one boundary: retirement cannot race an admitted operation, and queued ingress must recheck lifecycle before worker-side core entry. Refused construction leaves earlier exact owners intact and service initialization consumes the canonical failure without bypassing its cleanup. The lifecycle history fact and the runtime bootstrap transaction share one durable opening boundary, including process-crash recovery and genuine never-opened retries. If startup cleanup also fails, the original typed refusal and immutable owner retry answer remain primary; the actual secondary failure is retained, exact unclosed resources remain with the service lifecycle, initialize stays held, and existing shutdown retries that same cleanup without a new scheduler. Failed WASM teardown is CLEANUP_REQUIRED, not STOPPED.

raft-rs-runtime-application-transaction.description: The Ready owner and application transaction owner must agree on the durable point from which recovery may replay without duplicating application effects or splitting applied progress from ConfState. Current host-held observations and lifecycle-fenced participant admission are part of the same recovery boundary: the existing release queue retains bounded observation debt without duplicating runtime reconstruction policy or release authority; after ENABLE, one passive applied-position observation per current replica consumes the original bounded deadline and re-reads canonical facts before the existing final census; the canonical resume owner revalidates current handler, service and registry before OPEN. A failed nested control release retains only bounded own-data string observations of its missing fact, phase and reason; unavailable diagnostic detail cannot replace the original refusal or decide authority. Deadline expiry before dependent ENABLE leaves its admission closed without erasing a prior control origin; a new no-origin continuation requires current authorization. After a lost committed ENABLE answer and intact restart, missing current control keeps admission closed while the existing retry retains recovery responsibility. Seed registration acquisition and participant release run inside the existing registration phase and scheduler boundary, so an expired committed release still cleans every acquired registration resource. Failed cleanup reports a frozen observation alongside the unchanged primary refusal, retains exact failed service and SQL engine objects, and discharges only the object whose native shutdown and required handler retirement succeeded. Bootstrap shutdown joins its current attempt and retries a rejected attempt through the same cleanup owner. A retained committed origin survives cleanup but grants no missing SERVICES placement identity on the next actual startup.

partition-raft-operation-port.description: The raft-rs operation-port owner and the PartitionService consumer must agree on the exact frozen semantic port and its typed outcomes, with no node/control fallback and no second consensus runtime on either side.

spread-cure-transition-authorization.description: The mint and the receiving guard must agree on one authorization record: what the policy owner states, the learner decodes, evaluates and logs.

partition-session-transaction-store-pers.description: The participant's staging owner holds no SQLite transaction across requests - each validation is one synchronous transaction that rolls back - exactly so the rs-raft store's persistence admission never refuses a consensus write because of a participant session.

partition-write-answer-retry-classificat.description: The write-answer owners and the consumers that retry or re-send a write must agree on one classification of each answer: its code and its text say the same, but for the unknown outcome, which only a caller carrying its entryId routes again.

committed-bootstrap-stamp.description: The leader-read producer and target/raft consumer must agree on one canonical committed bootstrap stamp, including its fail-closed transport and shape boundary.

replace-owner-membership-observation.description: A change to how a replica announces, relays or answers its configuration, leader or term must keep the REPLACE owner's wakes, majority-current leader authority, completion and named handoff correct; a change to the owner must keep using only decoded consensus observations.

public-binding-table-policy-merge-decisi.description: The table-policy mutation owner and live split/merge decision owner must agree that the public Binding harness's nonvacuous split children are merge-ineligible before exact one-child versus two-child routing is proved.

partition-replication-record-physical-st.description: The durable workflow record must accept the exact attempt, fence, and payload before one PartitionService worker begins; transport acknowledgement without handler processing cannot bridge the two owners.

storage-reservation-operation-and-retry-.description: The reservation owner may adopt an operation-derived hold only when the replica_operations owner proves the exact immutable generation is still non-terminal. Insertion and authoritative reconciliation consume the operation mutation owner single existing retry deadline; temporary operation-authority loss retains the exact hold and redrives only through the canonical transition and dispatch gate, including after restart.

message-group-learner-authorization-cons.description: The existing repository observes exact issued ADD_LEARNER intent and current host-bound holder/recipient facts; the group-admission owner consumes that observation before reserving the permanent peer identity and invoking the semantic port. The native runtime alone decides term/configuration/lifecycle/generation freshness and proposes. This does not authenticate transport, settle the operation from a proposal reply, or grant CREATE.

message-group-learner-delivery-lifetime.description: The current socket/local delivery lifetime stays with RouterConnectionAuthorityOwner. The issued-learner consumer requires its host-only context; the existing native turn rechecks the same predicate after queueing and immediately before proposal. Revoking delivery does not cancel the durable issued action or prove global metadata atomicity. No physical CREATE is admitted.

message-group-committed-learner-origin.description: Existing committed application and permanent identity owners retain exact managed learner origin atomically; the queued historical read and versioned checkpoint validate that origin. Missing evidence remains unresolved; no current CREATE or reissue authority.

message-group-learner-outcome-recording.description: Same-turn native historical origin and committed membership witness feed one exact existing operation-row CAS; preserve terminal debt and old execution fences; current CREATE and successor issuance remain separate.

message-group-registered-learner-read.description: Actual registered recipient and retained workflow turn bind invoked callback/router, delivery and native lifetime through guarded repository submission; owned discovery (restart scan, periodic sweep, replicated-row wake) recovers membership debt by operation ID through the same recorder with an explicitly hosted witness. Preserve UNKNOWN after submission; no atomic lease/boot revocation or CREATE/successor permission.

snapshot-receiver-lifecycle-staging.description: Snapshot staging consumes a lifecycle-owned preparation answer without being allowed to mint or retire live runtime authority.

replica-host-cleanup-custody.description: The existing host retains exact unreleased service objects independently of active routing. Failed CREATE/restart and host shutdown use the same instance cleanup owner; typed failure retains custody, retries do not retarget successors, and pending cleanup bounds replacement admission without granting CREATE or storage-deletion authority.

wasm-writer-v1-application-completion.description: WASM delivery/lifecycle and application/result ownership jointly define exact completion, replay, bounded retirement and creation identity.

service-instance-selection-resource-stat.description: Immutable command/catalog lineage and conditional row application share one request, outcome and exact-state predicate. No local serialization or projection can choose a winner. Physical lifecycle release is still a separate unconnected obligation.

service-consensus-original-intent-admiss.description: Original intent/admission persistence and exact instance resource CAS are one ordered interaction. Lost replies retain original identity; generic physical creation remains unavailable for bound descriptors until the physical lifecycle is composed.

service-consensus-retained-native-bootst.description: Original full creation identity, physical CURRENT admission, exact retirement custody and ordered projection/journal debt are one owner interaction under U1 v3 and its addenda. The manager/driver consumes physical facts without deriving them from memos or booleans; the physical owner retains every admitted cleanup through shutdown. CLOSED or exact RETIRED plus unavailable history establishes physical finality only. A stopped projection owner performs no write, so its result cannot discharge the original journal. Native C6 custody and restart witnesses pair both sides; production A5 projection completion is not supplied by their direct writer.

runtime-service-bound-creation-route.description: The exact retained-plan handler, canonical execution gate and full-origin wake matching consume the same physical-currentness and retirement/debt contract supplied by manager, runtime, driver and physical custody owners. U1 v3 supersedes last-row-wins and current-memo authority: old origins retain their own journals and cannot retarget a successor. Gate/observer identity, immediate CURRENT projection fences, raw physical FINAL and unresolved STOPPED/journal debt change and are reviewed together. Real C6 restart and custody cases pair those owners, while bound-route consumer cases cover acknowledgment and bounded request observers. Production A5 retained-to-applied behavior is explicitly outside this proof. The bound REMOVE operation witness follows real RF3 publication through exact endpoint withdrawal, full-origin native retirement, successor grant refusal and failed-close custody/retry. Its component SQLite metadata and same-process transport do not certify cross-host authority or generic catalog activation.

runtime-service-legacy-removal-authority.description: The runtime handler and its bootstrap binding consume the original REMOVE operation through the dispatch service and existing repository strict-read and absence-classification owners. OWNER_RPC_REQUIRED and requireAbsenceConfirmation must remain paired: an unresolved owner read cannot become absence. Unavailable authority leaves cleanup retryable. A late authorization answer or queued STOP cannot admit physical work after its local memo is replaced; a late STOP result cannot overwrite the successor memo. Generic REMOVE retains its admitted memo while executing and releases only its exact execution entry when the attempt settles. Handler and strict-dispatch witnesses cover these consumer guarantees with a scripted repository; they do not prove native authority execution.

participant-release-bounded-completion.description: Fresh seed and CREATE delegate completion to the client under checked original-input, guard and clock-order contracts.

original-preparation-native-history.description: Original preparation consumes current validated native history before its application callback and at the final native effect cut.

participant-origin-native-history.description: One read snapshot binds participant origin bytes and the durable origin row to native applied, committed and local ranges without applying any command.

original-foundation-producer-observation.description: The retained observer matches the actual original foundation producers and normal applied SQL/outcome/CDC owners; pending work replays normally and no observation changes debt or opens startup.

cdc-source-native-delivery.description: The source/progression and recipient/transport owners preserve exact occurrence and whole-vector correspondence, bounded lifetime and actual cleanup while distinguishing provisional progress from native afterCommit authority for source acknowledgement. The approved interaction contract owns this boundary; test registration is not runtime proof or package acceptance.
